todo_line: - [ ] 002 Implement and focused-test the Messaging `RequestGroupAccess` composite command: derive requester, club, destination, subject, body, and club-hosted add URL server-side at the stable authorization checkpoint; resolve Admin Group recipients; dispatch existing `SendMessage`; propagate its result; and leave general web composition unchanged.
outcome: Messaging accepts a narrow RequestGroupAccess intent for an active same-club member outside a custom group and, at a stable authorization checkpoint, dispatches one fixed ordinary Admin root message with current Admin recipients and the club-hosted targeted-add URL.
scope: Add a plain application-layer `Memba.Messaging.Commands.RequestGroupAccess` intent and a public `Memba.Messaging.request_group_access/2` orchestration API. Keep caller-owned input to stable `message_id`, authenticated `club_id` and requester person identity, and target `group_id`; derive every message field server-side.

Within the existing stable-checkpoint pattern, call accepted `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3`, require an active same-club requester and custom-group target, and reject a requester who already currently participates in that target group.

Derive the destination as `SystemGroups.admin_group_id(club_id)`, resolve current Admin recipients through the existing authoritative Membership recipient path, and preserve ordinary sender delivery/follow semantics when the requester independently belongs to Admin.

Build a root `SendMessage` whose sender is the resolved requester, audience is Admin, subject is `Access request: <group name>`, and fixed plain-text body identifies the resolved requester, group, and club and contains `MembaWeb.ClubSite.url/2` for `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id`.

Dispatch only the constituent `SendMessage` through the existing Messaging application path after the successful checkpoint and propagate its normal `:ok`, execution-result, and error outcomes. Do not perform provider handoff inline.

Add focused tests for the successful ordinary Admin conversation and fixed URL/content; Admin-only current recipients; requester remaining outside the target group; forged extra sender/audience/content facts having no effect; invalid, missing, cross-club, built-in, inactive, and already-participating targets producing no MessageSent; stale-projection departure rejection; ordinary behavior for a requester already in Admin; and exact dispatch-result propagation.
Update Messaging's existing public-API/no-CRUD inventory test only as needed to recognize the new intent API while retaining its current architectural assertions.
scope_exclusions: Do not route RequestGroupAccess through `Memba.Messaging.Router`, add it to the aggregate command registry, persist a request, or add request events, status, deduplication, approval/denial, schemas, projections, or migrations.
Do not change the Message aggregate, SendMessage event model, recipient-fixing semantics, async provider delivery, conversation access, or sender-follow rules.
Do not relax or repurpose `send_club_message_as_current_member/2`, the member composer, or inbound email posting policy; general non-Admin web composition to Admin must remain unavailable.
Do not implement email HTML action rendering or text-template changes owned by task 004.

Do not implement the Request access LiveView action, targeted-add route or confirmation flow, welcome behavior, acceptance steps, feature-tag changes, or placeholder assertion updates owned by later tasks.
Do not edit `todo.md`, `plan.md`, ADRs, project documentation, or planner-owned delivery artifacts; only return the required worker result through the workflow's normal result artifact.

references.facts: Implementation Plan step 1 and the acceptance criteria define a server-owned composite request, stable authorization ordering, fixed Admin root message and recipients, ordinary SendMessage dispatch, and unchanged general composition policy.
RequestGroupAccess is handled in the Messaging application layer and is not routed or persisted as its own aggregate command; the stored body carries the ordinary club-hosted targeted Members URL.

The approved message copy identifies the requester, group, and club, uses subject `Access request: Board`, and links to `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id`; task 002 stores plain text and does not implement styled rendering.

Accepted task 001 returns authoritative same-club membership, custom-group, person, club, and current participation summaries with typed rejection reasons; consume this public API rather than Membership schemas or projections.

These are the established stable ordering, authoritative recipient construction, fresh delivery-ID, and normalized dispatch-result patterns. Build the request-specific SendMessage directly within that pattern rather than calling generic projected-audience composition.
The existing root command carries caller-generated message identity, resolved sender/audience/content, and pre-resolved recipients; only this constituent command belongs in the Messaging router.
Build the absolute club-hosted URL from the resolver's server-owned club slug and the typed group/person IDs. A verified route is not yet available because task 006 owns route creation.
Existing tests demonstrate Admin recipient resolution, root Admin access, stable-checkpoint stale-membership rejection, authoritative recipient selection, and projector lifecycle helpers.
Resolve recipients before SendMessage dispatch so MessageSent and delivery creation remain one existing aggregate decision.
Messaging depends only on Membership's public APIs and does not query Membership aggregate or projection storage directly.
The Club write model is authoritative for current club membership and Admin role facts.
Use current participation and fix recipients at posting time; later changes do not rewrite already-created deliveries.
Use supervised deterministic test-process synchronization and do not use sleep-based projector coordination.

constraints: Treat `message_id` as the stable caller-generated identity for uncertain retries; do not generate a replacement during orchestration.

Do not accept or trust caller-supplied sender, Admin destination, recipients, names, slug, membership identity, participation claim, subject, body, or URL. Extra map keys must not alter server-derived facts.

Keep authoritative eligibility resolution, current-participation rejection, Admin destination and recipient derivation, and SendMessage construction inside one successful stable-checkpoint callback; dispatch afterward so a later departure has the existing documented race semantics.
Use `SystemGroups.admin_group_id/1` and current authoritative Admin participation. Do not identify Admin by display text or use stale projected recipient membership.

Do not specially exclude the requester from recipients: an ordinary requester outside Admin gets no Admin delivery/access/follow, while an existing Admin requester retains normal Admin rights and behavior.
The successful result confirms command acceptance, not provider delivery or group admission; requesting must not mutate target-group membership.
Only fixed plain text is in scope. Safe HTML button recognition and rendering remain task 004.
Do not use `Process.sleep/1`; reuse existing deterministic projection/subscriber synchronization.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, acceptance suites, or another unscoped full-suite command in this packet.
completion_evidence_required: Return all changed paths and the public RequestGroupAccess input shape in `.delivery/latest-worker-result.json`; explicitly state that RequestGroupAccess was not added to the Messaging router.
Report the exact fixed subject/body shape and an example generated targeted-add URL, identifying which values came from the accepted authoritative resolver.

Name the focused tests proving Admin-only current recipients, requester non-membership after send, forged extra fields having no effect, built-in/cross-club/inactive/already-member rejection without MessageSent, stale-projection departure rejection, and existing-Admin requester behavior.
Show that successful dispatch produces the ordinary MessageSent/Admin write-access/delivery event shape and that requested returning/error outcomes propagate without synchronous provider delivery.
Record each focused validation command, exit status, and test/failure counts; list any unresolved issue without broadening into later todo obligations.
